provinces: Ca Mau (former Ca Mau, Bac Lieu); Vinh Long coast (former Tra Vinh, Ben Tre); Can Tho coast (former Soc Trang)
assets: Ca Mau farmed about 595,000 t of shrimp in 2025 (594,851 t; over 435,000 ha, about 40% of area); aquafeed mills C.P. Ca Mau 124.8 kt, Haid/Sheng Long Vinh Long 650 kt, De Heus Vinh Long 168 kt; planned green H2 about 118 kt/yr (Tra Vinh 24 kt with 182.5 kt NH3 and 195 kt O2; Ben Tre 24 kt; Bac Lieu 70 kt); Ca Mau 1,740 MW wind approved and up to 10 GW offshore potential; Dinh An Economic Zone; Bac Lieu shrimp hi-tech agriculture zone (418 ha, feed and biological products in scope); Ca Mau gas-based fertiliser plant (CO2, ammonia); shrimp processing by-products
missing_pieces: No green H2 plant built (Tra Vinh at fence and gate stage, May 2026); no legal track for offshore wind 'for new energy'; hi-tech zone stuck on land procedures; no pilot fermentation or feed-trial site on the coast (trial sub-centre is in Can Tho city); no CO2 volume or purity data; subsidence about 1 cm/yr and salinity; Ca Mau peninsula falls below sea level this century in every groundwater pathway, so 25-year plants need raised, surface-water sites
fitting_plays: T2 functional microbial feed for shrimp (now); T6 duckweed on effluent; T3 bulk microbial protein after 2030 on sugar shipped from Tay Ninh; frontier: hydrogen-oxidising bacteria feed protein co-located with electrolysers using by-product O2 and NH3 (demo 2032 to 2035, scale 2040 to 2045); methanotrophs on biogas (low fit)
horizon: T2: 2027 to 2030; power-to-protein demo: 2032 to 2035 if H2 is built; scale: 2040 to 2045
signposts: Electrolyser FID and construction at Tra Vinh, Ben Tre or Bac Lieu; a decree or PDP8 amendment giving new-energy offshore wind a legal track; land allocated and a feed or biologics tenant signed in the Bac Lieu zone; new Ca Mau and Vinh Long provincial plans naming a hydrogen or bio-industrial zone; a shrimp feed mill signs a microbial-protein offtake; InSAR subsidence staying above 1 cm/yr (watch)
source_ids: HUB-04; HUB-05; HUB-11; HUB-12; HUB-15; HUB-16; HUB-17; HUB-22; FTG-01; FTG-27; FTG-28; CLM-13; CLM-14; IND-45; IND-46
notes: A 10 kt/yr protein plant would take 6.9 kt H2 (29% of Tra Vinh design output), 29.5 kt CO2, 2.4 kt NH3, 32 kt O2 and 0.64 to 0.83 TWh (hub_calc.py). Tra Vinh's by-product O2 alone covers about 61 kt protein. Candidate, not a forecast.

hub: Mekong river belt: pangasius, rice and university hub
provinces: Dong Thap (former Dong Thap, Tien Giang); An Giang (former An Giang, Kien Giang); Can Tho (former Can Tho, Hau Giang); inland Vinh Long
assets: Pangasius about 1.74 Mt (2025), Dong Thap about 35% (about 0.61 Mt, our calc); 2026 to 2030 public investment in concentrated farming for Dong Thap, An Giang, Can Tho; aquafeed mills De Heus Can Tho 240 kt, Sunjin Hau Giang 126 kt, Uni-President (former Tien Giang), Cargill (Dong Thap, Can Tho); rice straw power potential An Giang 470 MW plus Dong Thap 190 MW (about 26% of national); rice bran and broken rice; pangasius by-products (62 to 67% of fish); Can Tho University (860 places/yr in 3 programmes); Region I aquafeed trial sub-centre; Hau Giang hi-tech agriculture zone 5,200 ha; breweries (Masan Hau Giang, Heineken Tien Giang)
missing_pieces: No pilot fermentation; no cheap-power or H2 advantage (Tien Giang H2 project 5.3 kt only); straw competes with biomass power, mushrooms and fodder; pangasius farms face 2 m flood levels at +50 cm sea level (mostly after 2050) and salinity in coastal units; groundwater restrictions
fitting_plays: T2 (pangasius and shrimp functional ingredients); T6 duckweed; T9 fungal foods on rice bran and broken rice; T10 rice protein; side-stream microbial protein on rice hydrolysates; by-product meal upgrading; frontier: lignocellulose (straw) biomass fermentation after 2035
signposts: Can Tho University or a mill opens a shared pilot fermenter; Hau Giang zone admits a feed-ingredient tenant; pangasius mills publish trials of novel ingredients; straw collection reaching 70 to 100% on the low-emission rice area (Decision 1490 milestones); MAE cluster or innovation centre sited in Can Tho
source_ids: HUB-12; HUB-13; HUB-14; HUB-18; HUB-27; HUB-28; INF-15; INF-28; IND-46; IND-47; CLM-20; NT-092
notes: Strongest research and buyer base in the delta; weakest energy. Best near-term site for feed trials and side-stream plays.

provinces: Tay Ninh (former Tay Ninh, Long An); with Dong Nai (former Binh Phuoc) cassava areas
assets: 68 starch factories, about 61,000 ha cassava and 6.4 Mt/yr root capacity in former Tay Ninh; cassava pulp (largest cluster) and starch-wastewater biogas; border imports of roots and chips; Saf-Viet (Lesaffre) yeast and VNVC biologics (former Long An); Daesang starch; highest southern irradiance (1,868 to 2,002 kWh/m2/yr); most vacant industrial land in the south (occupancy 60.9% vs 86.1% in HCMC, Q2 2026); named in 2026 to 2030 pangasius investment; Long An 249 t H2 pilot proposal
missing_pieces: No third-party glucose or hydrolysate supply in Tay Ninh (Vedan's is in Dong Nai); starch prices tied to Chinese demand; Cambodian root supply near exhaustion (early 2026); cassava mosaic disease; no concentrated CO2 or H2; the QNT S-ALT 2050 cassava need (5.4 Mt roots) equals 84% of former Tay Ninh root capacity, so a national sugar route cannot rest on Tay Ninh alone
fitting_plays: T4 cassava starch to fermentation sugar hub; T3 bulk microbial protein; T2 on sugar; T7 via tolling; T9; methanotrophs on starch-wastewater biogas (low)
signposts: A starch group invests in glucose or hydrolysate for sale; a foreign biomass-fermentation firm signs a Tay Ninh site; the new Tay Ninh provincial plan names a bio-industrial park; cassava root price and Chinese starch imports; mosaic-disease area in Tay Ninh and Dong Nai
source_ids: FS-03; FS-01; FS-14; COST-21; IND-17; FTG-18; HUB-04; HUB-13; CLM (cassava signpost); QNT-model
notes: A 20 kt/yr protein plant on cassava glucose needs about 252 to 303 kt roots a year, 3.9 to 4.7% of former Tay Ninh root capacity (hub_calc.py; yield assumptions stated there).

assets: Southern inter-regional renewable centre (Ninh Thuan, Binh Thuan); highest irradiance; Ninh Thuan 1 and 2 nuclear (4.0 to 6.4 GW, 2030 to 2035); hydrogen studies in Ninh Thuan and a 20 kt proposal in Binh Dinh; over 30% of national shrimp postlarvae (45 bn PL, 460 hatcheries); seaweed and a spirulina lead; Nha Trang University, RIA3, Pasteur Nha Trang, IVAC; Uni-President aquafeed (former Ninh Thuan)
